Compute composite score for cell groups

compute_composite_score.Rd

Computes a composite score by performing Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) between the deconvolution features of a cell group and the TFs of its module. The score is the weighted sum of the (scaled) features of the cell group, with the weights of the first canonical component. As the sign of CCA weights is arbitrary, the score is oriented so that it is aligned with the TF module: a positive score means that the sample is on the active side of the module for that cell group. The score therefore increases with the features of the cell group when they are positively related to the module, and decreases with them when they are negatively related.

Usage

compute_composite_score(
  cell_group,
  module_group,
  tfs.module.network,
  batch = NULL
)

Arguments

cell_group

A numeric matrix of cell deconvolution features for a cell group (samples x features), with sample names as row names. The module score and TF activities of tfs.module.network are matched to these samples by name; every sample must be in the network.

module_group

Character. Name (color) of the TF module the cell group was built from; must match a column name of the module matrix in tfs.module.network exactly.

tfs.module.network

Output of compute.WTCNA() (single- or multi-cohort).

batch

Optional vector with the cohort of each sample, in the row order of cell_group. It is treated as categorical: per-batch means are regressed out of the cell group features, the module score and the module TFs before the CCA.

Value

An unnamed list of two elements:

  • [[1]]: Numeric matrix (samples x 1) with the composite score, i.e. the scaled cell group features projected onto the first canonical component, oriented to be aligned with the TF module.

  • [[2]]: Projection parameters used to score new samples: xcoef (canonical weights of the first component), train_means and train_sds (column means/SDs used for scaling). The sign of xcoef follows the orientation of the score. train_means is NULL when batch correction was applied: new samples are then centred on their own means, as each training cohort was.

Details

The CCA is reliable only when the number of variables (features of the cell group plus TFs of the module) is well below the number of samples. When it reaches the number of samples, the first canonical correlation is 1 whatever the data, the weights are not unique and the score is decided by numerical noise (it can change completely with the sample order or a tiny change in the data). Large modules with few samples (e.g. cross-validation folds) are the most affected.

Examples

data("network.tuto")
data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
cell_groups <- construct_cell_groups(network.tuto, deconv_subgroups.tuto)
#> 20 of 764 features were not assigned to any cluster by the tree cut and are not part of any cell group (blue: 6, pink: 2, red: 2, yellow: 8, black: 2)
group <- names(cell_groups$Composition)[1]
module <- sub("^Dendrogram_(.*)_group_.*$", "\\1", group) # TF module of the cell group
features <- deconv_subgroups.tuto[[1]][, cell_groups$Composition[[group]], drop = FALSE]
score <- compute_composite_score(features, module, network.tuto)
head(score[[1]])
#>                         [,1]
#> SAM7f0d9cc7f001  0.039984111
#> SAM4305ab968b90 -0.133680921
#> SAMcf018fee2acd -0.026703505
#> SAMcc4675f394a1  0.061549350
#> SAM49f9b2e57aa5 -0.082696177
#> SAM2e7aa8fa0ab3 -0.004501591
